•mucus accum in sinus ← edematous mucosa (USU viral URI) → 2° bact infect - maxillary sinus MC
•erythematous · engorged nasal mucosa w.o intranasal purulence
facial pain or P worse w bending down & leaning forward
•watery · serous or purulent d/c · alt smell · dental pain · ear pain or P · fatigue - foul odor & dental pain = best clin predictors
•sx >10d or worsening w.in 10d after initial improvement (vs viral) - uncomp resolves w.in 2wks
•comp: frontal bone osteomyelitis (Pott puffy tumor) · preseptal or orbital cellulitis · septic cavernous sinus thrombosis · ext into meninges or brain
•noncontrast (coronal screening) CT: ⍉response to abx · comp dental infect · sus intracranial involvement or CSF rhinorrhea
•intranasal corticosteroids (mometasone) - esp if also allergic rhinitis & abx ⍉indicated
•rapid worsening of sxs after initial improvement
•severe sx or IS - mild sx <10d → observation
•sinus aspiration (specialist): severe HA or facial pain · toxic · orbital or intracranial comp · refractory to abx · recurr · IS - pain relief or identify pathogen
mast cell his release ← allergens (pollen · dust · mold)
- mediators: his · prostaglandins · leukotrienes · PAF · bradykinin - sensitization → sx USU require several yrs of exposure
- seasonal: MC pollen & spores - spring: tree pollens & flowering shrubs · summer: flowering plants & grasses · fall: mold & ragweed
- perennial (year-round): MC pet dander · household mites · dust · air pollution
- firstborn · birth during pollen season · maternal smoke during 1st yr of life · serum IgE >100 IU/mL b4 age 6
- Hx of asthma · atopic derm & sinusitis
- assoc w nasal polyps · asthma & ASA sensitivity (Samter triad)
- can → bronchiolitis but USU only in children w chronic lung dz
: nonallergic & noninfectious dilate of the blood vessels (rapid temp Δ · strong smells · humidity · spicy food) - ⍉classically assoc w asthma
- nasal congestion/obstruction · itching (eyes · inner ear · nose · throat) · eye tearing · postnasal drip · cough
- young children: repeatedly snort · sniff · clear throat & cough instead of blowing nose
- untx: poor sleep → fatigue · malaise · irritability · poor concentration · worse school or athletic performance · low self-esteem
- intermittent (<4d/wk or <4wks) or persistent (>4d/wk or >4wks) - year-round or seasonal
- mod-severe: sleep disturb · impaired ADLs · impaired school or work · bothersome sx
: ± periorbital bluish discoloration (allergic shiner), nasal salute
- infraorbital edema & darkening (allergic shiners ← subcut venodilation)
- Dennie-Morgan lines: accentuated dark lines or folds below lower eyelids → allergic conjunctivitis
- transverse nasal crease ← allergic salute (rubbing & pushing up tip of nose)
- early onset: highly arched palate · open mouth breathing · dental malocclusion
- clear rhinorrhea in nasal passage or posterior pharynx
- retracted TM or serous fluid behind TM ← ETD or nasal mucosal swelling
: clin Hx - may confirm w skin testing or allergen-specific IgE
- routine labs (CBC · CMP) norm - ↑eos & total IgE in only 30-40% → ⍉sensitive enough to confirm

- IN corticosteroids (fluticasone · beclomethasone · budesonide): shrink hypertrophied nasal mucosa & polyps · enlarge nasal airway · improve drainage · ↓risk of bact sinusitis - ≥2wks to peak efficacy
- 2nd-gen antihist (loratadine · fexofenadine · cetirizine): more immediate sx control - may need to alt periodically esp perennial
- mild or episodic: 2nd-gen antihist · antihist nasal spray or glucocorticoid nasal spray (fluticasone) - QD or prn for exposure
- persistent or mod-severe: glucocorticoid nasal spray = tx of choice (most effective for all sx) - add nasal antihist spray &/or 2nd-gen PO antihist for further control
- glucocorticoid nasal sprays & antihist each most effective taken daily (vs prn)
- montelukast (LTRA): tx both allergic rhinitis & asthma
- antihist · mast cell stabilizers (cromolyn) · short-term decongestants
- cromolyn nasal spray: 30min b4 exposure - ideal for short exposures to specific allergens - less effective than IN steroids
- olopatadine (IN antihist): w glucocorticoid nasal spray for further control incl breakthrough sx
- diphenhydramine (1st-gen antihist): sedating · Q4-6h - ⍉for pts in school or w fatigue - major SE of 1st-gen antihist = drowsiness
- anticholinergics can be used for rhinorrhea

- avoidance & enviro control · exposure reduction: plastic covers on pillows & mattresses · animal products instead of synthetic materials · remove dust-collecting fixtures (carpet · drapes · bedspreads) · chg clothes & shower b4 bed · air purifiers & dust filters · nasal saline irrigation
- refractory or severe sx → refer to allergist for immunotx
